items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: “Jerry I can’t take it anymore I want to sell the record label.”

ctx.x: All right. So there used to be a record convention in Philadelphia. The name of the organization was NAIRD — N-A-I-R-D. National Association of Independent Record Distributors, and kind of at the center of that organization was Richmond Brothers which was a one-stop in the Philadelphia area. And so once a year, you know Indy record label owners would come into Philly and they would all come to my store, all of them, and look to see if I was carrying their records. It was really fun to see, you know, they would…

Allen Pittman put out, on his Theresa label, two of the great Pharaoh albums ever. Despite that, and he had put out more than two, but there were two two-record sets that he put out that became classics in jazz and for Pharaoh Sanders. And despite that and putting out a series of great albums, he couldn’t take it anymore, losing money, getting screwed around by distributors, that kind of stuff. And Allen was a peaceful man. He was not the guy to collect money. “Give me my money or else,” that was not Allen…
No that’s great, I mean I completely agree with you on the arc of the recordings there in terms of him kind of coming back into his own a bit at that time.
